clue.text: Pass English by mistake

blocks.note: E is the standard abbreviation for English
a lapse is a slip or error

explanation.surface: Someone gets through an English exam only by accident.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to pass or elapse; the verbs are synonyms for time going by.

clue.text: Wild sheep ahead of us in ancient city

indicators.note: wild things are disordered and uncontrolled, so the letters run loose into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: A flock of feral sheep wanders ahead of tourists through the ruins of an old city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ahead of' places the rearranged animals before US in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephesus was a Greek, later Roman, city on the coast of Asia Minor, now ruins in Turkey.

clue.text: Metal bracket in corner on press

blocks.note: a corner is an angle
to press clothes is to iron them

explanation.surface: A metal bracket fixed into the corner of a printing press.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'on' means placed above, so the corner sits on top of the press.
explanation.definitionFit: Angle iron is a length of L-shaped steel used to make brackets and frames.

clue.text: Drove round centre of Kampala, exhausted

indicators.note: the centre of a seven-letter word is its fourth letter, the one kept here
going round something means surrounding it, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: drove, as in drove someone mad, means sent
the middle letter of Kampala

explanation.surface: A worn-out traveller after driving around the middle of Uganda's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Kampala is the capital of Uganda.
explanation.definitionFit: Spent means used up, with no energy left, a synonym of exhausted.

clue.text: Head of state rests fitfully — it's the pressure

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
fitfully means irregularly and in bursts, so the letters fall out of their order

blocks.note: first letter of state
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A head of state sleeping badly because of the pressure of office.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is mental or physical strain, which is a kind of pressure.

clue.text: Curious terrapins come to light

indicators.note: curious means odd or strange, so the letters appear in a peculiar new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Inquisitive turtles emerge into the daylight.
explanation.definitionFit: To transpire means for a fact to become known, i.e. to emerge or be revealed.

clue.text: The best selection of Chinese literature

indicators.note: a selection is a run of letters taken from the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: An anthology of the finest Chinese literature.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts at the last letter of Chinese and carries into literature.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite are the choicest or most distinguished members of a group.

clue.text: One-time sleeveless garment?

blocks.note: single means one
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A question about a vest worn only once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One-time' reads as 'former', but it splits into its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A singlet is a vest or sleeveless athletic top.

clue.text: Army officers to run eastern trading post

blocks.note: generals are senior army officers
taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: Senior army officers set to take charge of a trading outpost in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: A general store sells a wide range of goods, like a frontier trading post.

clue.text: What Harrow on the Hill appears to offer?

definitions.text: What Harrow on the Hill appears to offer?

blocks.clueFragment: What Harrow on the Hill appears to offer?
blocks.note: surface reading: a question about what a place in north-west London provides
setter's reading: Harrow is a famous public school, and being on a hill its schooling is literally elevated

explanation.walkthrough: Harrow School stands on a hill in Harrow on the Hill, a London district; schooling up a hill is literally 'higher'. Really it is a secondary school, hence 'appears'.
explanation.definitionFit: Higher education is university-level study, and a hilltop school seems to offer study at altitude.

clue.text: Frantic nurse, poorly prepared

indicators.note: poorly means unwell or badly done, so the letters before it are put out of shape

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
trained means prepared for a task

explanation.surface: A panicking nurse who was poorly prepared for the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poorly prepared' reads as one phrase, but 'poorly' works on nurse while prepared supplies the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrestrained means without control or restraint, as frantic behaviour is wild and uncontrolled.

clue.text: New sweaters worn by the lovers

indicators.note: something new is remade, so the letters are rebuilt in a fresh order
clothes worn by someone wrap around them, so the garments go outside the other piece

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: A couple in matching new jumpers.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged garments wrap around THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweethearts are a pair of people in love, i.e. lovers.

clue.text: Slippery creature? Female's not in touch

indicators.note: saying a thing is not in something means it is taken out of it

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female
to touch is to feel

explanation.surface: A slippery character, a woman who is out of touch.
explanation.walkthrough: Take F out of the word for touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Eels are famously slimy and hard to hold, the proverbial slippery creature.

clue.text: Petty quarrel about tail of cleaner fish

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter
about means around, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: a spat is a brief, trivial argument
last letter of cleaner

explanation.surface: A minor squabble over the tail of a cleaner fish, a reef species.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleaner fish' is a real kind of fish, but the definition is only the final word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprat is a small silvery fish of the herring family.

clue.text: Dramatist editor crossed

blocks.note: Ben Travers wrote the Aldwych farces
ED is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A playwright angered his editor.
explanation.walkthrough: Crossed looks like 'annoyed', but it means went across. Ben Travers was an English writer of stage farces.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to travel across something, so traversed means crossed.

clue.text: One who attacks salsa, anti-dancing?

indicators.note: dancing letters move around and change places

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who criticises salsa and is against dancing altogether.
explanation.definitionFit: An assailant is a person who assaults or attacks another.

clue.text: Total ingredients of concrete

blocks.note: first meaning: a sum or whole formed by combining
second meaning: the sand, gravel or crushed stone mixed with cement

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a builder's tally of materials; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a sum total and the name for the crushed stone and sand in concrete.

clue.text: One conducting a survey amongst tent dwellers?

definitions.text: One conducting a survey amongst tent dwellers?

blocks.note: surface reading: a person going door to door collecting opinions
setter's reading: tents are made of a heavy cloth, so the pollster is jokingly a person working the cloth shelters

explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as the name of the tent fabric plus an agent ending, so a door-to-door pollster seems to be someone who visits campers.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvasser goes round asking people's views or votes, which is conducting a survey.

clue.text: Reticent about opening of revue put on in Greater London borough

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
about means around, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: coy means shy or reticent
first letter of revue
to don clothes is to put them on

explanation.surface: A shy performer opens a revue staged in a London suburb.
explanation.definitionFit: Croydon is a large borough in south London, part of Greater London.

clue.text: Avid listener brought round good piece of Elgar

indicators.note: bringing something round another means wrapping it about it
a piece of a word here is just its first letter

blocks.note: an ear is what listens
G is the abbreviation for good
first letter of Elgar

explanation.surface: A keen concert-goer won over by a fine work of Elgar.
explanation.walkthrough: EAR goes around G plus E.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means keen and enthusiastic, the same sense as eager.

clue.text: One wearing flared skirts takes a chance

indicators.note: flared things spread out of their original shape, so the letters are reworked
one wearing clothes is inside them, so this piece goes within the garment

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone daring enough to wear flared skirts.
explanation.definitionFit: To risk it is a phrase meaning to take a chance on something going wrong.

clue.text: Mythical monster in Windsor Castle

indicators.note: in means the letters are sitting inside the words that follow

blocks.note: letters spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A legendary beast lurking in the royal residence at Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: An orc is a monster of myth and fantasy, best known from Tolkien.

clue.text: Musical game

blocks.note: first meaning: the 1980s stage musical by Tim Rice with the men of ABBA
second meaning: the board game of kings and queens

explanation.walkthrough: 'Musical game' reads as one thing, like musical chairs, but each word is a separate definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess is the board game and also the title of a well-known stage musical about a championship.

clue.text: Spain still cold?

blocks.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)
still means not moving

explanation.surface: A question about whether Spain is still having a cold spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still cold' looks like a remark on weather, but still is a piece and cold, in the sense of unfeeling, is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold person shows no feeling, so is emotionless; the question mark flags the less obvious sense.

clue.text: Operatic work, not quite typical

indicators.note: not quite means falling a little short, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: normal means typical

explanation.surface: An opera that is not really representative of its kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is Bellini's opera about a druid priestess.

clue.text: Outfit tries again to involve little Sarah in full-scale practices

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it in, so one piece is enclosed by another

blocks.note: a dress is an outfit
a court rehears a case when it tries it again
Sal is a short form of the name Sarah

explanation.surface: A costume is being retried to fit young Sarah before the full performance.
explanation.walkthrough: SAL goes inside the second piece, just before its final S.
explanation.definitionFit: A dress rehearsal is the final full run-through of a show in costume, a complete-scale practice.

clue.text: Inventor returned for end of rugby match

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the name is read backwards

blocks.note: Thomas Edison, inventor of the phonograph and light bulb

explanation.surface: An inventor came back for the end of a rugby game.
explanation.definitionFit: No side is the referee's traditional call ending a rugby match, the equivalent of full time.

clue.text: The last word in extremely long-drawn-out sad song

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of a word, its first and last letters
in means one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: the outermost letters of long-drawn-out
amen ends a prayer, so it is literally the last word

explanation.surface: The final words of a slow, drawn-out sad song.
explanation.walkthrough: AMEN goes inside the two outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A lament is a mournful song or poem expressing grief.
